market_summary: Amsterdam has more bikes than people and bike-light theft is a running joke among commuters and students. Cheap clip-on lights from supermarkets and AliExpress dominate; they are treated as disposable. Premium brands sell durability but not replacement. Nobody sells peace of mind as a subscription, so the category is open. Fines for riding without lights add urgency in autumn.

competitors.name: HEMA / Action clip lights
competitors.weakness: Dim, break fast, stolen constantly, no support

competitors.name: Knog
competitors.weakness: EUR 40+ per set, painful to lose, no replacement

competitors.name: Swapfiets
competitors.weakness: Only covers their own bikes; lights are an afterthought

personas.name: Daan, 31, commuter
personas.who: Rides Noord to Zuidas, wants zero admin

personas.hook: Never get fined for a light again

insights: Light theft is a shared Amsterdam experience; jokes about it travel fast on social
The autumn fine season (October) is the natural launch moment
Subscription framing works when it removes a chore, not when it adds one
Students respond to cheeky tone; commuters respond to zero-hassle promises
message_to_team: Bram, research is in: light theft is a shared Amsterdam joke and nobody sells replacement as a service. Two personas, Sanne the student and Daan the commuter. October fines are our timing hook.
